Twice the size, for clips up to 720p

Doubles the width and height of the clip and draws in new detail. Works on clips up to 720p. On a recent top phone, 10 seconds of 540p video take about 5 to 10 minutes; mid-range and older phones take much longer. Best on recent phones with a strong graphics chip.
Four times the size, for clips up to 360p

Makes small clips, like old phone videos, four times wider and taller. Works on clips up to 360p. On a recent top phone, 10 seconds take about 2 to 4 minutes; budget phones can take over half an hour.
More detail at the same size

Brings back fine detail and keeps the size. Quick sharpening is instant and works on every phone. The AI version looks much better but is slow: about 15 minutes for 10 seconds of 720p video on a recent top phone, so use it on short clips. Works on clips up to 1080p.
Sharper faces, the rest stays as it is

Finds faces looking at the camera and sharpens only them, blending the result softly into the picture. It does not change how anyone looks. About a minute for 10 seconds of video on a recent top phone; mid-range phones take a few times longer.

Each clip shows its own frames. A 30 fps clip in a 60 fps export shows every frame twice, so motion can look a little stepped.
The new in-between frames mix the two nearest frames like a quick cross-fade. Fast to export; fast motion can look ghosted.
The app follows how each part of the picture moves and draws real in-between frames. Smoothest motion, but the export is slower and very fast motion can smear at the edges.
Low leans on the nearest frame, so there is less ghosting. Medium mixes the two frames evenly. High also mixes in the frames around them for the softest motion. Quick on every phone.

Low tracks motion roughly and is the quickest; it suits Basic phones. Medium is the usual choice for Good phones. High tracks finer detail with more passes for cleaner edges; it is slow, so keep it for Fast phones or short clips.

Smears every frame of a video clip along its motion, like a camera shutter: Low 90°, Medium 180° (the usual film look), High 360°. It also works when a clip already has the export frame rate. It has to track motion, so it takes about as long as Optical flow Medium.
